title: Lesson 55: Scaling Agent Workloads: Horizontal Scaling, Queues, and Worker Pools
description: Adding capacity to an agent system by running more workers, decoupling producers from consumers with a queue, and sizing the worker pool off queue measurements within rate and budget limits.

questions.question: Per the lesson "Scaling Agent Workloads: Horizontal Scaling, Queues, and Worker Pools", why does a worker need to be stateless for horizontal scaling to work?
options: Stateless workers are the only kind that can call a model provider
If each request's context lives in the worker's memory, only that worker can finish it, so adding workers does not spread the work
Stateless workers avoid consuming any CPU or memory while idle
State is an anti-pattern in all distributed systems
questions.explanation: The lesson states that for horizontal scaling to work, state must live somewhere addressable by any worker, so any copy can pick the work up. Context held in one worker's memory makes it the only one able to finish the request.

questions.question: The lesson describes four useful things a queue does for an agent system. Which set does it name?
options: It stores model weights, caches prompts, batches tokens, and compresses context
It absorbs bursts, enables scaling by queue depth, isolates failures, and lets throughput rise by adding consumers
It replaces the orchestrator, removes the need for retries, and eliminates worker crash recovery
It reduces latency per request, raises quality, and removes the need for rate limiting
questions.explanation: The lesson assigns the queue four roles: absorbing bursts as backlog instead of failure, providing the queue-depth signal for scaling, isolating worker failures so a task is picked up again, and letting throughput rise by adding consumers without redesign.

questions.question: According to the lesson's worker pool guidance, which queue signal tells you to add worker capacity?
options: A steady empty queue with all workers idle
Queue wait time climbing past a few seconds while depth grows, meaning workers cannot pick work up fast enough
A high completion rate with low CPU usage on the workers
The provider's latency budget being under target
questions.explanation: The lesson says a wait time climbing past a few seconds means workers cannot pick work up fast enough, so you add capacity. An empty idle queue is the signal to scale down, not up.
